    input clk;

    input [7:0] head;  // Head pointer (8-bit address of the first node)  
    output reg [7:0] current_value;  // Current node value  
    output reg end_of_list;  // Indicates if the end of the list is reached

- `start_connection`: triggers the transition from IDLE to CONNECTING.
- `confirm_connection`: transitions from CONNECTING to CONNECTED.
- `disconnect`: transitions from CONNECTED or CONNECTING to DISCONNECTED.
- `reset`: resets the state machine to IDLE.

The state of the Bluetooth module should be represented with a 2-bit value:
- 00: IDLE
- 01: CONNECTING
- 10: CONNECTED
- 11: DISCONNECTED

module bluetooth_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start_connection,
    input wire confirm_connection,
    input wire disconnect,
    output reg [1:0] state
);

    // State encoding
    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, CONNECTING = 2'b01, CONNECTED = 2'b10, DISCONNECTED = 2'b11;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start_connection) state <= CONNECTING;
                end
                CONNECTING: begin
                    if (confirm_connection) state <= CONNECTED;
                    else if (disconnect) state <= DISCONNECTED;
                end
                CONNECTED: begin
                    if (disconnect) state <= DISCONNECTED;
                end
                DISCONNECTED: begin
                    if (start_connection) state <= CONNECTING; // Can start connection from DISCONNECTED
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple memory allocator that can allocate and free memory blocks of a fixed size. The allocator should be able to handle requests for memory allocation and deallocation. The output indicates the success or failure of the operation.
code:
module memory_allocator(  
    input clk,  
    input reset,  
    input [1:0] request_type, // 00: free, 01: allocate  
    input [3:0] block_index,  
    output reg success  
);  
    reg [15:0] memory; // 16 blocks of memory  
    initial begin  
        memory = 16'b0000000000000000; // All blocks are initially free  
        success = 0;  
    end  

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin  
        if (reset) begin  
            memory <= 16'b0000000000000000; // Reset memory  
            success <= 0;  
        end else begin  
            case (request_type)  
                2'b01: // Allocate  
                    if (memory[block_index] == 0) begin  
                        memory[block_index] <= 1;  
                        success <= 1;  
                    end else begin  
                        success <= 0;  
                    end  
                2'b00: // Free  
                    if (memory[block_index] == 1) begin  
                        memory[block_index] <= 0;  
                        success <= 1;  
                    end else begin  
                        success <= 0;  
                    end  
                default: success <= 0;  
            endcase  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

                    tx <= 0;  // Start bit  
                    state <= DATA;

    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [3:0] data,
    input load,
    input shift,
    output reg [3:0] q
);

        q <= 4'b0000;  // Reset the shift register
    end else if (load) begin
        q <= data;     // Load the input data
    end else if (shift) begin
        q <= {1'b0, q[3:1]};  // Shift right and fill with 0
    end
end

endmodule

    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [4:0] temperature,
    output reg shutdown
);

description: Design a simple Watchdog Timer in Verilog. The Watchdog Timer should reset itself when a "kick" signal is received within a specified timeout period. code:
module watchdog_timer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire enable,
    input wire kick,
    output reg timeout
);
    parameter TIMEOUT_PERIOD = 5; // Number of clock cycles before timeout
    reg [2:0] counter; // 3-bit counter for timeout

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            counter <= 0;
            timeout <= 0;
        end else if (enable) begin
            if (kick) begin
                counter <= 0; // Reset counter on kick
                timeout <= 0; // Clear timeout
            end else if (counter < TIMEOUT_PERIOD) begin
                counter <= counter + 1; // Increment counter
            end else begin
                timeout <= 1; // Set timeout flag
            end
        end
    end
endmodule
